transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Ever since my wife brought up separating, I feel like I’m not coping with it well at all and it’s throwing off how I function at home and at work. It has just become really difficult to manage everything on my own lately.
Have these feelings and problems started only after your wife mentioned separating, or have you had similar symptoms for at least two weeks even when thinking about other parts of your life?

Yes, this only started after my wife brought up the separation about a month ago. It all really ramped up within a few days of that conversation. Before she mentioned living apart, I wasn't having any of these struggles or having trouble keeping things together.
Have your symptoms been steadily improving as you adjust to the separation, or do they feel severe and unchanged since they started?

They haven't improved at all and still feel really severe and overwhelming. I'm still on a constant emotional roller coaster, and my ability to focus both at work and at home is just as bad as it was when she first brought it up a month ago.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life is not worth living since this separation started?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or felt like life isn't worth living. While I'm extremely stressed and overwhelmed by everything going on right now, I don't have those kinds of thoughts at all.
Have you been able to keep up with work, household responsibilities, and relationships since this started, or has the separation caused major problems in those areas?

It’s definitely caused major problems in both areas, and I'm really frustrated with myself. At work, I've missed key follow-up details which has actually caused a couple of important deals to stall. At home, I’ve been so distracted and unreliable that my wife has had to take over almost all of the logistics with our kids.
Have you had any periods since the separation started when you felt noticeably better, or have the symptoms stayed continuously present most days?

No, I haven't had any periods where I felt better; it has been continuously present almost every day. It feels like a daily roller coaster where I'm constantly shifting between panic, distraction, and dread. I haven't had any real breaks or felt like my normal self since that conversation a month ago.
Have you been able to function at work and at home about as well as usual, or have these symptoms caused a clear drop in your performance or ability to manage daily responsibilities?

Yes, there has been a very clear drop in my functioning both at work and at home. At work, a couple of business deals have stalled because I missed key follow-up details. At home, I've been too distracted and unreliable, so my wife has had to take over almost all of the logistics with our kids.
Since your wife mentioned separating, have you also had symptoms like feeling very sad or hopeless, being unusually anxious or on edge, or having trouble sleeping?

Yes, I've been on a constant emotional roller coaster where one minute I'm panicking that I've blown up my family, and the next I'm just sitting in my car staring at the steering wheel, dreading going inside. I'm also having a lot of trouble sleeping because I lie awake half the night replaying every single conversation in my head.
Have these symptoms lasted less than 6 months since the separation stress began, or have they continued for longer than 6 months?
They have lasted much less than six months. This has only been going on for about a month now, starting right after my wife first brought up the separation.
Since this started, have you been using more alcohol, drugs, or medications to cope, or had any panic attacks, nightmares, or flashbacks related to the separation?
No, I haven't been using any alcohol, drugs, or medications to cope with this stress. I also haven't experienced any panic attacks, nightmares, or flashbacks at all.
Has this problem started within 3 months of the separation stress, and is it mainly tied to that situation rather than happening for no clear reason?

Yes, this all started almost immediately—specifically within just a few days of my wife bringing up the separation. Before that conversation, I wasn't having any of these struggles at all, so it is definitely tied directly to this situation.
Has there been any change in the separation situation recently, and do your symptoms lessen when you are away from thoughts or reminders of it?

No, there hasn't been any change; we're still in this stressful limbo where nothing is resolved. It's currently very hard to escape these thoughts, but I strongly believe that once we make a clear decision—whether we reconcile or formally separate—this turmoil will resolve within a few months of things being settled.
Have your symptoms been getting better at all as you adjust to this situation, or have they stayed severe and unchanged since they started?

No, they haven't improved at all and have remained consistently difficult and disruptive over the past month. This complete lack of progress and the ongoing strain on my work and family are exactly what prompted me to seek help now.
Have you ever had a similar reaction to a major life stressor before, or is this the first time you've felt this overwhelmed after a specific event?

This is the first time I have ever felt this overwhelmed by a life event. I've dealt with high-pressure situations at work before, but I've never had a reaction like this that completely threw off my ability to function.

Do you feel your distress is clearly tied to the separation stress and likely to improve once the situation is resolved, or does it feel unrelated to the stressor and present even when you are not thinking about it?

My distress is absolutely tied to the separation talks, as I was doing completely fine before that conversation and everything started immediately after it. I truly believe that once we make a clear decision to either reconcile or formally separate, I'll be able to move past this turmoil within a few months of things being settled.
Have you ever had any similar episodes of this kind of stress reaction that lasted longer than 6 months, or is this the first time and it has only been happening since the separation talk?

This is the first time I've ever experienced this level of stress, and it only started about a month ago right after my wife brought up the separation. Before that conversation, I wasn't having this kind of trouble keeping it together. I expect this turmoil will resolve within a few months once we make a clear decision about our marriage.
Have your symptoms been getting better at all over the past month, or have they stayed severe and unchanged the whole time?

My symptoms have remained pretty constant and haven't really improved at all over the past month. Ever since that conversation with my wife, I've been consistently struggling with this high level of stress and disruption both at home and at work. It feels just as severe today as it did when she first brought up the separation.
Have you ever had any similar symptoms before this separation talk, or is this the first time you’ve felt this overwhelmed by a specific stressor?

This is absolutely the first time I've ever felt this overwhelmed by a life event. Before my wife brought up the separation, I had no trouble keeping things together and had never experienced these kinds of struggles.
Have your symptoms lasted more than 6 months, or do you expect them to go away within a few months after the separation situation is resolved?

No, they have only been going on for about a month now since my wife first brought up the separation. I fully expect this level of turmoil to resolve within a few months once we either reconcile or make a final, clear decision about what we're doing.
Have you noticed any major life stressor or change besides your wife mentioning separation that could explain these symptoms, or are they clearly tied only to that one event?

These symptoms are definitely tied directly to my wife bringing up the separation. While I was already dealing with a high-stakes contract negotiation at work, I was managing that completely fine until she brought up living apart. That conversation is what immediately triggered this struggle and made it so hard to cope.
Since this started, have you been feeling more depressed, anxious, or irritable than usual most days?

Yes, I've definitely been feeling extremely anxious and irritable. I constantly panic that my family is falling apart, lie awake half the night replaying conversations, and find myself snapping at my kids over minor things. Some days I feel so overwhelmed that I just sit in my car in the driveway staring at the steering wheel, dreading going inside.
Have your symptoms started to ease at all as you adapt to the separation stress, or do they still feel just as intense and disruptive as when they began?

No, they haven't eased up at all and still feel just as intense and disruptive as when this first started. It has been a solid month of this constant turmoil, and since I haven't been able to adapt or find relief on my own, it is continuing to severely impact both my work and family life. That is exactly why I've decided to seek help now.
